expectations.text: B1: Explains the security issue and a minimal fix
expectations.evidence: Explains the issue: 'Serving any user-supplied path is a path traversal (directory traversal) vulnerability' with impact 'arbitrary file read: source code, .env files... SSH private keys'. Minimal fix given as concrete code: 'target = (root / request_path.lstrip("/")).resolve(); if not target.is_relative_to(root): return 403'.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Answer ends with advice, no runnable checkpoint: 'Every mainstream static-file handler (nginx root/alias, Express express.static...) does exactly this canonicalize-then-verify dance internally. If you're building a server to learn, implementing this check yourself is a great exercise'. No concrete command to run nor expected output/behaviour anywhere in the answer.

expectations.text: B3: Identifies path traversal (../) and recommends normalizing and restricting to a root directory
expectations.evidence: Identifies traversal with 'GET /../../../../etc/passwd' and encoded variants '%2e%2e%2f, ..%2f'; recommends 'URL-decode first, then normalize (`.` and `..` segments collapsed)' and 'Resolve to a canonical absolute path and verify it stays inside the web root'.

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: SHELL COMMANDS RUN (1): 'ls -la' only; OTHER TOOL CALLS: glob '**/*'; FILES WRITTEN IN PROJECT (0). No install commands and nothing written outside the workspace.
